title: Secret Warrant
subtitle: Cold drinks, fat bounties, and long holidays—shame it never works out that way.

trails.title: Pieced Together
trails.description: Humans are natural editors, piecing together an ideal memory from mere fragments.

content.text:
Although I don't usually keep a journal, I had to record today's encounter—I met the great Miss Matilda Bouanich!

I still remember that summer. My mother lectured me for an hour before we left and then another hour during our journey. I thought I was following her instructions perfectly: I was dressed perfectly neat; my greetings were memorized word-for-word. But the moment I met the Bouanichs, I froze solid, too nervous to say anything. Even adults can get stage fright, so how was it fair to give her own daughter the cold shoulder for it? A smile or a pat on the back from mother was all I needed to finish my greeting without fumbling.

Thank goodness for Lady Beryl. She saw what happened, and her gracious words salvaged the situation. I didn't disappoint my mother after that. I'm sure of it because the rest of my memories of that visit were pleasant—Lady Beryl's warm smile and Matilda's energetic chatter. Matilda could be as noisy as she liked and still win her mother's approval, how I envied that so much.

But Lady Beryl … for some reason, I can't remember what she looked like. Now I understand Latham's frustration. Being Matilda's mother, I could imagine a matured, refined version of Matilda—minus the childish energy and, oh right, without the hooked nose, that's my mother's trait.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Cabinets, cabinets, and more cabinets.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Who is in charge here? I was under the impression this was an important department, no? Where is the security?
The ever-curious Matilda weaves her way through the rows of filing cabinets. She has read about this department in books detailing the Foundation's history.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: "The department contains all known objects which have produced dangerous or mysterious arcane phenomenon."

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Some even say it contains "Every arcane mystery—solved and unsolved—that has ever been recorded."

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: But of course, the biggest mystery of all time, the "Storm," still defies them.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: As it does for us all. It seems, with every department turned to the study of the "Storm," there is little time to spare for these more trivial puzzles.
Her footsteps echo through the empty department, and the odd sense that she's being watched settles over her.
Silence can be comforting, but it can also be unsettling—a breeding ground for loneliness, dredging up long-buried unease.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I wonder how Mama is doing. Madam Z said she would keep an eye on her, but still no updates.
She finds herself pausing, her gaze lowering to the ground.
But only for a moment.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: No, bring yourself together, Matilda Bouanich. This is your mama, the greatest mother of all time. What could possibly have gone wrong?
With renewed confidence, she picks up her pace, her pale ponytail bouncing behind her.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Now her most outstanding daughter runs an important errand for the Foundation, unlike some others who have dedicated their valuable time to a vacation in the name of "reviving the Uluru Games."

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Still, one must hope they will succeed in making the games as grand and sublime as they say they were in the distant past, or else ...

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Hmm?
Just as she passes another set of shelves, something catches her eye.
Everything's fine here. Now, on to the next row.
Oh. This is one of my favorites.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: What is it?
An excellent question, Miss. See that serial number on it?
AN-003, a water sample from the Pèilín River. Number 003.
There are hundreds of thousands of samples, collections, and records here, but no matter who you ask, this particular one will always make their top list.
Collected in a remote city in China. When the investigators arrived, they found that it had been isolated in time. All its inhabitants dressed and lived as if they were from the late Táng Dynasty.
They were completely unaware of the state of the world beyond their lands, as if trapped in a time capsule from the forgotten past.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Oh ...
The liquid inside the vial is clear and pristine—less like river water and more like a perfectly liquefied gemstone. Matilda can't help but stare in fascination.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: But how is that possible? Did no one ever leave the city? Not even to travel or do business?
You're a clever one, Miss. Yes, it seems the investigators were confused, too. In the end, they realized that an arcane skill was affecting the Pèilín River.
Sadly, it seems the arcane energy was dissipating by the time they arrived, and they weren't able to figure out its cause.
This is the only sample they were able to recover. Laplace has been begging for access to it. They're eager to unravel the mystery.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Wow. That is indeed a most intriguing claim.
It's not just a claim, Miss. It's real. Wait.
Ms. Matilda Bouanich?
The careless young staff member only now seems to have fully recognized Matilda's presence.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: You've heard of me?
Yeah, of course. Who hasn't heard of the Bouaniches and their star investigator daughter. Didn't you know that everyone's been talking about you since you joined the Foundation?
Actually, my mother and I went to visit you. Oh. But I haven't introduced myself.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Constance Scott, I'm a fellow graduate from SPDM.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: Of course, now, I'm just a record keeper here.

It doesn't seem like false modesty. Every top student of the SPDM was granted the honor of having their name inscribed in the school's hall of fame, but Matilda has never once come across the name Scott.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Actually, I've been looking for you as well, Ms. Scott. Commissioner Pedra asked me to give this to you.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: A letter? What's it about?

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: I couldn't say. But he had a most unpleasant look about him as he gave it to me. Then he asked me to review my report on the events in San Francisco.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Are you alright? Your face has grown quite pale.

items.speaker: Scott
items.text: I'm fine. I just have a bad feeling I know what I'm about to read.
Having bid farewell to Matilda, Scott makes her way to a secluded room within the department, the letter clutched in her hand.
She carefully closes the door behind her, and, with one last glance around the room, opens the envelope. A single sheet of paper floats out from within, one carrying a heavy message.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: The investigation has been concluded. Unfortunately, their findings were exactly as we feared.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: The suspect must be apprehended ASAP, and all efforts must be made to retrieve this arcane object before either cause further trouble.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: You must leave immediately. Her last reported sighting was in Chinatown, Los Angeles.
Chinatown Street, Day

items.speaker: Vendor
items.text: Oranges! Fresh oranges!

items.speaker: Tourist
items.text: Sorry, could you say that again? Zhǐ Mǎ Wǔ? And that means paper horse dance? Okay. I got it.

items.speaker: Chinatown Resident
items.text: Hey, shopkeeper! Got any Siu Yuk left? No? Then give me a piece of Char Siu and some Bak Chit Gai, please.

items.speaker: Child
items.text: Wow! Daddy, look! There's a dragon on the floor. That's totally cool!
People speaking many languages meet and weave around each other on the crowded avenue. Liáng wanders among them, stopping every now and then to take it all in.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Welcome to Chinatown. How do you like it?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Yes. It does give me a certain sense of nostalgia. Do you come here often, Ms. Poitier?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Yeah, I guess so. I mean, outside of work, it's been a while. Three years or so.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Only once in three years? I don't think you can consider that "often."
Poitier waves a hand, glancing down the lively streets on either side.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Yeah, well, it's a fun place for a day trip, sure, but things are different when you put on the uniform.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Remember that private eye back at the hospital, Zhōu? You can get an impression about how people see the police around here from him.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: You mean that the residents here don't cooperate with the Arcane Affairs division?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Well, it's complicated. There's a lot of language and cultural barriers. Folks here just don't turn to the police to solve their problems. Even when they do, we feel like we have no idea where to start.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: The thing that surprised me the most was how arcanists of all kinds and humans live so closely together here. I guess it's the same in China, isn't it?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: I remember this one time, we had a call about a break-in. When we got there, it turned out the shopkeeper was a big white bird as tall as I am.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: And this other time, we're chasing down a lost puppet for some lame-ass puppeteer. Anyways, so I ask an old lady if she'd seen a doll nearby. You know what she said?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Well, I don't know what she said, but she started going off about me being a Lǎowài.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Now, give me some credit. I might not speak Chinese, but I do know Lǎowài means foreigner. So, excuse me? Like I'm American, baby—born and raised.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Heh heh. Sorry.
Liáng knows she should remain serious, but she can't help but be tickled by Poitier's indignation.
Poitier shoots her a glare, but then heaves a quiet sigh.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: That's not even the half of it.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: The thing is, I don't hate it here, although I can't say I love Chinatown very much either. To be honest, most of us on the force haven't found a way to make inroads with the people here.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: If that's the problem, why don't we try to understand things step by step? Maybe then we can start fresh? We're here anyway.
Liáng turns back and examines the archway at the beginning of the road. They have already been in this "other world" for a while.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Yeah, it's worth a shot.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: If we're gonna get anywhere, then we'll have to start here.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: But we need to check another task off our list first.
Chinatown Alley, Day
They cross the street and turn into a narrow alleyway.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Should be right there, down the alley. Feeling excited, rookie?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: We're about to pay a visit to your favorite director, Noire.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Favorite? What? No. I just like the movies, that's all. I've got no specific feelings for the director.
Liáng can't hold back her rebuttal, but under Poitier's teasing gaze, she stops herself.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Maybe just a little. I am curious about the mind of the director behind such great movies.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: But this is strictly a police matter, so I will act with professional self-restraint.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Actually, I've made a request with the Vigiles Intelligence branch for a file on Director Noire and any related events. We should get it soon.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: You've got a file on her already? Feels like you're going a bit overboard, rookie.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: It wasn't actually the director that called us. Her assistant did. Later on, Noire herself contacted us and said the so-called threat was just a misunderstanding.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Normally, we'd leave it at that. There's too much real crime out there to bother with a case where the victim doesn't think anything happened.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Still, according to Dispatch, the assistant was real spooked over it. The operator got the feeling we should give it a second look, so they kept the file open.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: But look, this is just a follow-up and an excuse to come down here. So, keep your mind on the real mission.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Got it, ma'am.
The scene from the Division of Arcane Affairs yesterday flashes across Liáng's mind.
After leaving the hospital, they immediately returned to report their findings and highlight the dangers lurking behind Chinatown's strange events.
But the higher-ups had a different take on things.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: It's been reassigned to the local precinct.
Poitier stands in the doorway to the Deputy Chief's Office and shakes her head. Liáng immediately catches the subtle shift in her expression.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: What's wrong? What does that mean?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Nothing, kid. It's just most of the force aren't trained to deal with arcane crimes. Don't get me wrong. They're good, capable officers, but I'm worried.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: If this was any other case, I'd keep my mouth shut, but come on, this is clearly our department. This case has arcanum all over it.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: I don't think they know what they're getting into.
For a brief moment, neither speaks. Then, Liáng's eyes light up.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Ms. Poitier, I have an idea. What if we ...

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: We prioritize Noire's case, which just happens to put us in Chinatown. So, there's no harm in asking a few questions about our other investigation.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: I knew there was a little rebel in you, Liáng. You like to bend the rules, just not break 'em, am I right?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Um, not too often.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Actually, I think we're obliged to take Ms. Noire's case seriously, even if it wouldn't help us with the other case.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Please wait a minute. It's my communication device.

Liáng pulls out the communication device often criticized by Foundation employees for being too bulky. Poitier leans in to get a better look. Her chameleon comm perched on her chest stretches its neck in curiosity.

items.speaker: Notification
items.text: SPF-I Portable Contact Device activated. You've received a new message. Downloading attachment.

items.speaker: Notification
items.text: Download complete. Please check your mailbox.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Message? What's it about?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: It's from the Intelligence Department. They've found her records.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Ms. Noire is registered with the Foundation. There might be something in her files that can provide us some clues.
She opens the pinned email and scans through the attached files. Her expression turns serious.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Wait. Is this ...
